title: Timesteps and the window
summary: A timestep is one moment. The window is how many moments you keep.

terms.definition: The clock tick of a discrete spiking network. Membrane, leaks, and spikes update once per timestep.
The span of timesteps over which you count spikes or wait for the voltage to settle.

cards.text:
The simulation walks forward one moment at a time.
That moment is a timestep.

lines: The neuron tips on step 1 and step 3.
It is quiet on step 2 and step 4.
In this window the count is 2.

cards.text:
A longer window makes a rate steadier, and the answer later.
The timestep is the moment. The window is how many you keep.

question.prompt: Tips on steps 1 and 3 of a 4-step window. How many tips are in the window?
question.why: Two of the four steps contain a tip.
question.simpler: Count tips inside the window. Do not count the window length itself.

recall.question: What is the difference between a timestep and a window?
recall.answer: A timestep is one moment. A window is how many moments you keep.

deeper.note: Rate codes, converted networks, and direct training all pick a window. The choice is part of the model. Gerstner’s Neuronal Dynamics treats the discrete step in chapter 1.

paper.title: Neuronal Dynamics
paper.section: Section 1.3, discrete time as a sequence of small updates.
